The lazy DFA cache makes the worst-case match test go from 7.06 s to 0.32 s. Excellent.

Let me verify that the cold-cache worst case is still OK (the first match builds the DFA). It's 0.32 s for 128 matches, so the first one dominates... Actually the cache is per _Nfa (per pattern), and all 128 matches use the same pattern and the same string (all 'a's of length 512)! So it's a single DFA path. Let me test with distinct strings to force cold paths.

Let me modify the test to use varied strings.

Actually, let me measure the true worst case: distinct strings for each match. Let me test with 128 distinct strings of 512 chars, matching a 128-char "a*"*64 pattern — different strings would follow different DFA paths (some dead immediately).

Hmm, but the documented bound is what it is. Let me test with strings that are all 'a' but of varying content to exercise different DFA states.

Let me do a quick sanity check of the cold-cache cost: use strings of random 'a'/'b' chars.
